Eastern Bay local government proposal to be considered by councils next week

For immediate release – 31 July 2026An outline proposal setting out a case for an Eastern Bay of Plenty Unitary Council was published yesterday (Thursday, 30 July 2026) as part of the agenda papers for council meetings next week.The proposal, developed jointly by Kawerau District Council, Whakatāne District Council, and Ōpōtiki District Council, will be considered by Whakatāne and Opotiki District Councils on 4 August; and by Kawerau District Council on 5 August.

Tribute to Malcolm Campbell - our esteemed former long-serving Kawerau Mayor and BOPRC Eastern Bay Councillor

-from Her Worship the Mayor of Kawerau Faylene Tunui, on behalf of all current and former Kawerau councillors and staff:Nā koutou i tangi, nā tatau katoa / when you mourn, your tears are shed by us allIt is with a grief-stricken heart that I share the passing of former Mayor of Kawerau Malcolm Campbell MNZM JP.The community of Kawerau knows Malcolm well, because he was one of us.   Malcolm was born in 1952. He was one of the early pupils at Kawerau Central School and Kawerau District High (as it was known then).

Ministers turn out in force as Kawerau cements its clean energy position

23 March 2026  Government ministers were out in force in Kawerau as Conservation Minister Tama Potaka cut the ribbon on Cool-Safe’s new refrigerant destruction facility while Minister of Trade and Investment Todd McClay inaugurated Eastland Generation’s TOPP2 geothermal power plant.  “Eastland Generation and Cool-Safe are helping cement Kawerau’s position as a centre for sustainable energy and kaitiaki taiao | environmental stewardship,” said the Mayor of Kawerau Her Worship Faylene Tunui.

Four councils investigate best future water options for region

Kawerau District Council, Rotorua Lakes Council, Whakatāne District Council and Ōpōtiki District Council are working together to investigate the next best steps forward for community water services in the sub-region. The councils have been meeting regularly since the pōwhiri and heads of agreement signing last year.

Steam bore issues impact Maurie Kjar Aquatic Centre

There are ongoing issues from the geothermal steam bore that provides hot water to heat the Maurie Kjar Aquatic Centre. This is disappointing as the current steam bore was drilled in November 2021, with the funding support of Trust Horizon, which was greatly appreciated by Council and the community.At a depth of 79 metres, the bore accesses naturally hot geothermal water at approximately 145 °C that flows under pressure (called artesian).
